sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Pop star aims to use legal process to name ‘wrongdoers who hide in the shadows and wreak technological havoc with impunity’ Ariana Grande has filed a lawsuit against hackers who she alleges have stolen unreleased music, as well as private photos and video footage, and sold them online. Grande filed the lawsuit in a Los Angeles court on Monday. It doesn’t name the hackers, who are referred to with the generic name John Doe. Grande will look to have them identified during the legal process “in order to hold them accountable for their invasive and reprehensible conduct”, the lawsuit reads. Continue reading...

sources.name: The New York Times
sources.summary: The singer says that for years members of her inner circle have been the victims of hacks aimed at stealing unreleased music, photos and videos.
